তারিখ: ১৫ জ্যৈষ্ঠ, ১৪৩১ বঙ্গাব্দ/ ২৯ মে, ২০২৪ খ্রিস্টাব্দ

এস.আর.ও. নং ২১১-আইন/২০২৪/৬৩/কাস্টমস।- কাস্টমস আইন, ২০২৩ (২০২৩ সনের ৫৭ নং আইন) এর ধারা ২৬৩, ধারা ১১৯ এর সহিত পঠিতব্য, তে প্রদত্ত ক্ষমতাবলে, সরকার, জাতীয় রাজস্ব বোর্ডের সহিত পরামর্শক্রমে, নিম্নরূপ বিধিমালা প্রণয়ন করিল, যথা:-

Customs Act 2023: This Act provides the legal authority under sections 119 and 263 for the government to formulate new customs rules.
National Board of Revenue: The government is required to consult with the National Board of Revenue before exercising its rule-making powers under the Customs Act 2023.
S.R.O. 211-AIN/2024: This statutory regulatory order constitutes the formal instrument through which new customs rules are promulgated by the government.

Warehouse Goods Storage Duration Rules 2: These rules are formally titled the Warehouse Goods Storage Duration Rules 2024.
The rules are effective from the date specified in the order to fulfill the objectives of the parent Act.
Warehouse Licensing Rules 2024: These rules are applicable to all institutions that hold a valid license under the Warehouse Licensing Rules 2024.
Customs Act 1969: The rules are enacted under the authority of the sub-section of Section 263 of the Act to ensure its implementation.

Customs Act 2023: The term Act is defined as the Customs Act 2023 for the purpose of these rules.
Warehouse Storage Period: This term refers to the specific duration allowed for storing goods in various classes of warehouses as prescribed under these rules.
Bonded Enterprise for Domestic Consumpti: This refers to an enterprise that processes raw materials imported under bond facilities and supplies the finished products for domestic consumption upon payment of applicable duties and taxes.

Bonded Warehouse Operation: The period for storing goods in a bonded warehouse commences from the date of clearance of goods from the import customs house or customs station, or in the case of local sourcing, from the date of issuance of the Value Added Tax invoice by the supplier.
The maximum duration for storage in a bonded warehouse is established based on the specific category of the industrial or bonded entity.
Export-Oriented Industry: Goods imported by direct or deemed export-oriented industrial establishments may be stored in a bonded warehouse for a maximum period of twenty-four months.
Shipbuilding Industry: Goods imported by export-oriented shipbuilding industrial establishments are permitted to be stored in a bonded warehouse for a maximum period of forty-eight months.
Diplomatic and Duty-Free Bonded Warehous: Goods imported by diplomatic bond establishments, duty-free bond establishments, duty-paid bond establishments, and those managed by the Commissionerate are subject to a maximum storage period of twelve months in a bonded warehouse.
Customs Act 1969: This regulatory order prescribes storage durations for bonded warehousing as provided under sub-section (2) of section 119 of the Customs Act 1969.
Domestic Consumption Bonded Warehouse: Goods imported by bond establishments designated for domestic consumption or other similar bonded entities are limited to a maximum storage period of six months.

৪। ওয়্যারহাউসে পণ্য সংরক্ষণের মেয়াদ হ্রাস বা বৃদ্ধিকরণ।— (১) কোনো পণ্যের বা কাঁচামালের গুণগতমান অবনতি হইবার আশংকা না থাকিলে কমিশনার অব কাস্টমস (বন্ড) অথবা বোর্ড কর্তৃক ক্ষমতাপ্রাপ্ত অন্য কোনো কমিশনার অব কাস্টমস লিখিত কারণ উল্লেখপূর্বক, পণ্যের গুণগত মান অক্ষুণ্ণ থাকা সাপেক্ষে, ওয়্যারহাউসে পণ্য সংরক্ষণের মেয়াদ আরো অনধিক ৬ (ছয়) মাস সময় পর্যন্ত বৃদ্ধি করিতে পারিবেন।

(২) কমিশনার অব কাস্টমস (বন্ড) অথবা বোর্ড কর্তৃক ক্ষমতাপ্রাপ্ত অন্য কোনো... কমিশনার অব কাস্টমস এই বিধির উপ-বিধি (১) ও বিধি ৩ এ যাহা কিছুই থাকুক না কেন, কাঁচামাল বা পণ্যের গুণগতমান অবনতি হইবার সম্ভাবনা থাকিলে, প্রতিটি ক্ষেত্রে তিনি যেরূপ উপযুক্ত বিবেচনা করিবেন সেইরূপ যুক্তিসংগত সময়ের জন্য ওয়্যারহাউসে পণ্য সংরক্ষণের মেয়াদ হ্রাস করিতে পারিবেন।

Bonded Warehouse Operation: The customs authority may extend the storage period for goods or raw materials in a bonded warehouse for an additional fixed period, provided there is no risk of quality deterioration and the goods remain in sound condition.

The customs authority is empowered to reduce the storage period for goods or raw materials in a bonded warehouse if there is a risk of quality deterioration, allowing for a reasonable timeframe determined by the appropriate officer.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or any other customs official authorized by the National Board of Revenue is granted the discretionary power to approve extensions or reductions in the storage tenure of warehoused goods based on quality assessment and regulatory criteria.
National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue holds the authority to designate or empower specific Commissioners of Customs to manage storage duration adjustments for warehoused goods.

National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is empowered to consider applications for the extension of the storage period of bonded goods on a case-by-case basis.

The Board reviews recommendations from the Commissioner of Customs regarding extension requests, taking into account factors such as product quality, export capacity, audit compliance, and the absence of pending legal proceedings.
Bonded Warehouse Operation: Licensees may apply to the National Board of Revenue for an extension of the storage period if they fail to use the imported goods for manufacturing or other authorized purposes within the initially granted timeframe.
The extension process involves an on-site verification of raw material inventory and quality, and may include obtaining expert opinions to determine the suitability of extending the storage period.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or another authorized Commissioner is responsible for reviewing the status of the warehouse and providing recommendations to the National Board of Revenue regarding applications for storage period extensions.

National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is authorized to oversee the transition of existing regulations, orders, and decisions upon the commencement of new rules.
Existing instruments issued by the board are formally repealed, while actions taken under them are preserved and deemed valid under the new framework.
Commissioner of Customs (Bond): The Commissioner of Customs (Bond) is identified as an authority whose previously issued notifications, orders, and decisions are subject to repeal under these rules.
Customs Legislation: Upon the effective date of these rules, all prior notifications, orders, and decisions issued by the specified customs authorities are rescinded.

Notwithstanding the repeal of previous instruments, any actions already taken or initiated proceedings that remain pending will continue to be governed by the prior provisions as if the new rules had not been enacted.
